articleTitle: Improved peak shaving and valley filling using V2G technology in grid connected Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: During the last decades, the development of electric vehicles has undergone rapid evolution, mainly due to critical environmental issues and the high integration of sustainable energy sources. The large-scale integration of these vehicles will impact the operations and planning of the power grid. In this paper, we focused on an electric vehicle charging/discharging (V2G) (Vehicle to grid) energy management system based on a Tree-based decision algorithm for peak shaving, load balancing, and valley filling in a grid-connected microgrid. The main objective is to provide an optimal clipping strategy based on the use of EV as mobile storage means to reduce critical customer demand, fill off-peak periods by considering vehicle requirements, load demand, and electricity price variation. The study developed in MATLAB/Simulink is applied on a grid-connected microgrid that includes a grid-connected photovoltaic array, a variable hybrid load (industrial and residential), and an EV charging station that receives 10 vehicles during the day depending on the users' lifestyle. Two load peaks are expected during the day (one due to the start-up of industrial areas and another due to high consumption in the evening) are tested to see the behavior of the management system in peak reduction. The simulation results demonstrated the performance of the V2G technology in peak management applications. The analysis of the results proved the robustness of this solution in peak shaving during high demand periods and valley filling during off-peak hours by allowing a smoothing of the load curve and better exploitation of the micro grids.

articleTitle: A Nash-game approach to Blind Image Deblurring
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: Images are undeniably a vital part in our life, they are now used in all of kind of fields, hence, image processing became a must. Common image processing include image enhancement, restoration, encoding, and compression. Restoring is a process to improve an degraded image quality, to sharpen an image, and remove the noise. A major cause of image degradation is blur. There are many types of blur: motion blur, the most common, is a blur due to subject movement, or a camera shake. Blind deconvolution is the reconstruction of a sharp clean version of a blurred image without prior knowledge of the blur kernel (PSF) or the original image. In this paper, we will study the Nash game as a blind deconvolution technique for image deblurring, and we will test this method by presenting some numerical examples, and comparing it with other methods predefined in MATLAB, or existing in the literature.

articleTitle: Machine learning approach for predictive maintenance of transport systems
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: Transportation companies must face to a huge competition and must reduce downtime and the associated costs. This can be achieved through predictive maintenance (PM), which defines maintenance actions based on the health of the system and its environment. Relevant information can be extracted from massive data related to health prognosis and management (PHM) by applying artificial intelligence (AI) techniques. This paper proposes a Machine Learning approach to develop a prediction model based on a supervised learning by comparing several regression algorithms. The model is then applied to the Remaining useful mileage prediction of trucks tires for a transport application of dangerous substances.

articleTitle: New hybrid approach based on artificial neural networks for RFID network planning with random redundant antenna elimination
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) makes it possible to identify physical objects directly and unambiguously, as well as to be recovered, stored, transferred, and processed without a gap between the real and virtual worlds. Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology is one of the most widely used IoT technologies for locating and detecting objects in a variety of industries. The deployment of the RFID system led to the establishment of an RFID network planning (RNP) problem, which is based on satisfaction of some objectives such as network coverage, network interference and network redundancy, and the RNP issue is an NP-hard optimization problem in a vast deployment environment. The purpose of this paper is to propose and illustrate a new hybrid approach that combines the neural network algorithm and a new variant of the redundant antenna elimination algorithm to address with the RNP problem. Our experimental results applied on a widely used benchmarks show that our approach provides more accurate and cost-effective results that easily satisfy the most important criteria of RNP, and still guarantees a better deployment of the RFID network.

articleTitle: Drone Cyber-Attack: An Intrusion Detection Technique Based on RSSI and Trilateration
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: The drones or the Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are used in several fields: military, security, health, agriculture, transport, media. Several vulnerability studies on drones have shown that attacks are easily carried out over Wi-Fi or radio links [1]–[2]. In this paper, we will focus on an attack scenario through radio frequencies aiming to hijack the drone. Our approach, based on the Received Signal Strength Indication (RSSI) technique and the trilateration method, will allow the drone to ensure that the signal received is legitimate.

articleTitle: A new modified Bat algorithm for Air Traffic Flow Management
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: Air traffic is growing steadily while the available airspace remains roughly the same, which is why it must be optimally exploited. In this paper, we try to better manage arrivals in the approach area for Mohammed V Airport, given the saturation of this space, we propose to solve two new models [1] that make it possible to schedule traffic in a direction where the most efficient will be served, and so on, while harmonizing arrivals so that the aerodrome can receive aircraft continuously, We propose to solve the models using a modified Bat algorithm (BA), the proposed solution will allow us to increase the capacity of the airport and to better manage the approaching controlled space, as being a limited space.

articleTitle: Finite difference method for Perona-Malik model with fractional derivative and its application in image processing
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: In this work, we consider the Perona-Malik (PM) model with fractional derivatives and its application for image processing. This model is obtained from the standard PM equation by replacing the ordinary derivative with a fractional derivative. the numerical resolution of this model is based on the finite difference method, we analyse efficient numerical methods for the fractional model, and we give practical experiments with natural images which are showing that the fractional approach is more efficient than the ordinary integer one. the proposed model has good performance in visual quality and high signal to noise ratio (SNR)/ Peak signal to noise (PSNR)

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Warehouse Management: A conceptual framework
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: Warehousing industry is highly affected by trends of globalization and the increasing dynamics of product life cycles, which results in global supply chains. For warehouse management, a huge number of products needs to be delivered on time and at the lowest cost possible in order to provide desired level of customer service. Currently, a high amount of time and energy are spent to gather information about products and customers to be used to decide about the needed warehouse operations and to measure their performance. Therefore, this paper presents an approach to predict future warehouse operations as well as the measurement of performance using an integrated approach. The proposed approach includes four main stages: the identification of warehouse operations and KPIs, then the creation of warehouse operations and KPIs ontology, after the modelization of the ML model and evaluation, and finally the creation and the prediction of future warehouse operations and KPIs. Using machine learning, generic knowledge of warehouse operations and performance measurement could be extracted then used to predict future scenarios.

articleTitle: Deployment of RFID Readers Using a Robustness Multi-objective Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: RFID (radio frequency identification), or radio identification, is a technology that allows data to be saved and retrieved remotely on so-called RFID tags. It has many applications in many sectors. one of the widely known issues in the RFID technology community is the deployment of RFID readers problem. Therefore, in order to solve this problem, we propose a robust multi-objective approach to deal with uncontrollable parameters in the system by optimizing the main objectives: the coverage, the number of deployed readers, and the interference. The simulation results show the performance of our proposed approach in terms of robustness.

articleTitle: A Nonlinear Fractional Partial Differential Equation for Image Denoising
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: The image denoising is a key step in image processing. This step can be treated by nonlinear diffusive filters requiring solving evolving partial differential equations. In this work we propose a nonlinear evolving partial differential equation with spatial fractional derivatives in order to improve the denoising capability and to extend some existing results in image denoising. The discretization of the fractional partial differential equation of the proposed model is performed using the shifted Grünwald-Letnikov formula useful for constructing stable numerical schemes. The comparative analysis shows that the proposed model produces better or comparable quality of enhanced image than various well know and state of art techniques as well as several image analysis techniques.

articleTitle: A Distributed Digital Twin Architecture for Shop Floor Monitoring Based on Edge-Cloud Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: Throughout recent years, many “Smart Factory” concepts have been emerged to escort the current technological progress. Among these concepts, we found the Digital Twin which is a burgeoning technology that attracts great interests from academics and industry. Akin to other technologies, the power of Digital Twin can be strengthened by leveraging other technologies' benefits such as those of cloud computing and edge computing. First, to support the implementation of the Digital Twin for the shop floor monitoring, a conceptual architecture of the Digital Twin based on edge-cloud collaboration is proposed. This architecture is believed to enhance the real-time capabilities of the Digital Twin while dealing with the abundant amounts of manufacturing data. Moreover, the paper discusses how the microservices architecture can benefit the proposed Digital Twin architecture. On the other hand, in order to provide an underpinning to researchers on the Digital Twin topic, the paper sums up the description and an up-to-date output of the Digital Twin, highlighting four manufacturing application scenarios.

articleTitle: Multi-level Architecture Modeling of an Intelligent Energy Management Strategy for Battery/Supercapacitor Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: Given the negative environment impact of the traditional transportation technologies, a switching to electric vehicles has become a necessity to promote energy efficiency and generate less emissions, noise, and CO2. In fact, due to technological advances in battery technology, several electric mobility solutions were presented by vehicle manufacturers and automobile market. Despite this development, the performance of battery based EVs are still incapable to match ICE vehicles. At present, many promising researches have shown and proven that the integration of hybrid energy storage system (HESS), such as batteries/Ultracapacitor, Batteries/Fuel cells or Fuel cells/Batteries/Supercapacitors, can improve energy efficiency, reliability, aging and degradation of batteries. Therefore, the energy management strategy is an indispensable key to ensure the normal operation of the system and achieve the performance of the HESS and the vehicle. The aim of this paper is to model a multi-level architecture of intelligent energy management strategy for battery/Supercapacitor electric vehicle and simulate two levels of our architecture using MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: AI-based speed control models for the autonomous train: a literature review
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: The railway industry recently showed interest in the potential use of AI to render trains autonomous in order to reduce cost and improve security and performance. This paper focuses on the integration of AI into Automatic Train Operation (ATO) systems to control train speed. The objective of this paper is to present and analyze a review of the literature made in that context. The review is done according to a typology based on three axis: the inputs and objectives of the model, the AI method used by authors and last, the validation process. Our review shows that AI based approaches outperform classical approaches and that learning based methods are superior to rule-based systems. Meanwhile, the contributions present incomplete validation processes, difficulties to generalize the proposed AI method and last, a lack of use of perceptual data during decision making. This analysis enables us to draw some prospects relevant to the solving of the listed limitations.

articleTitle: Exploring applications of Machine Learning for supply chain management
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: In the current economic context, due to globalization, the trend of outsourcing/off shoring and the flexibility of distribution processes, companies have moved towards sourcing products from distant markets around the world in order to save production costs. This, in turn, has resulted in longer lead times for the production and supply of products, which has increased the uncertainty of demand. In fact, all supply chain processes are based on demand forecasting data, so methods to improve forecasting can increase the efficiency of the supply chain. Machine learning techniques, have recently emerged as an alternative to traditional methods, and have proven to be capable of solving demand forecasting problems. In this paper, we explore the bibliography of recent research of Machine Learning applications to supply chain and in particular demand forecasting. A total of 79 articles were reviewed and collected of two databases, ScienceDirect, and Scopus. The study demonstrated the power of machine learning algorithms over traditional demand forecasting model, and showed that neural networks where one of the most used algorithms in demand forecasting. Finally, the strength of machine learning techniques in solving demand forecasting problems in different areas, asserts its remarkable influence in improving the efficiency of the supply chain. This can encourage both decision makers and stakeholders to plan corrective actions based on machine learning applications to supply chain and demand forecasting.

articleTitle: Virtual and Augmented Reality in school context: A literature review
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: Virtual and Augmented reality has established itself in many sectors including education. The virtual is progressively entering the classrooms. MOOCs (Massive Open Online Course), those online interactive lessons available for all, are useful tools to complete the traditional school system. There are also more and more e-learning platforms that propose online lessons and follow-up for any student. Immersive contents appear as playful alternatives to traditional lectures. However, the integration of VR/AR equipment in classrooms raises questions. What place takes the augmented (AR) and virtual reality (VR) in the modern educational and teaching system? In order to be able to answer this important question, our article takes place as the result of a literature review on the field of virtual and augmented reality in education. Our objective, first of all, to deepen our knowledge domain in order to provide the necessary answers to « the main question », and, secondly, to identify principles that can guide the design of educational artifacts in virtual and augmented reality. The methodology of the literature review is based on the EPPI method (Evidence for Policy and Practice Information and Co-ordinating). Results will be presented by themes such as motivation, immersion, collaboration, and design.

articleTitle: Sustainable product development: the intersection of Design for X, Big Data and Industrial Internet of Things with fuzzy logic theory
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: The use of Industry 4.0 technologies has sped up the growth of production on which manufacturing systems are being turned into automated and connected ones. As a result of the complexity of products and the exponential change in consumer demands, the amount of uncertainties in today's technology and industrial environments is rapidly increasing. The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and Big Data (BD), in particular, have played an increasingly important role in the product development process (PDP) in a variety of industries, leading to value growth, competitive advantage and idea generation. Besides, to meet customer and sustainable requirements over the product Iifecycle, the PDP requires the use of Design for X (DFX) approach to integrate different factors X's, In this regard, this paper aims to combine knowledge from various fields into a detailed, realistic and holistic approach for the implementation and development of services and products using DFX techniques, BD and IIoT technologies. More clearly, this study uses fuzzy multi-criteri a theory to provide practitioners and managers with a guide to selecting the most important DFX techniques that consider quality attributes in product or service design while considering the advantages of BD and IIoT technologies.

articleTitle: An information system for the evaluation and capitalization of the product development knowledge
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: Product development is a complex multi-field project in which engineers with different specialties work together to achieve the same goal. In fact, with the growth of sustainability challenges, designing a new product with respect to cost, functionality, assembly, safety, reliability, quality, serviceability and environment issues have specific properties that directly affect the way knowledge is carried out. Thus, having an overview of a project or remembering the collaborative work of past projects is difficult for practitioners. Hence, the aim of this paper is first to present a project memory architecture (MemoDFRelevance) in order to structure, index and store all the relevant knowledge needed during the development of a product while considering different factors X (DFRelevance). Second, the paper describes also the development of a Web application (SmartDFRelevance) for the automatic evaluation and capitalization of the knowledge.

articleTitle: Blockchain application to improve Vendor management replenishment in Humanitarian supply chain
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: In some African vulnerable countries, the local service provider warehouses and government health facilities contain significant stocks of pharma products with low shelf life and not compliance with quality & regulatory standards. The stockpile is the consequence of donations from the global health institutions and pharma companies. If it's not properly managed and regulated, the expired pharma products may be reworked and sold as counterfeited drug to other neighboring countries or destructed with potential environmental pollution impact. To get rid of this problematic, the pharma companies, global health partners & local authorities should lead a deep digital transformation of the humanitarian supply chain. This paper investigates the VMR-based blockchain solution applied to the donation supply chain which leading to a transparent, reliable and authentic ecosystem. To reach this objective, we suggest a novel framework model based on blockchain and smart contract for managing the connections between the supplier, the global alliance and the local humanitarian service provider. We propose the new VMR architecture adapted to humanitarian supply chain. A use-case VMR application is presented along with a functional smart contract.

articleTitle: TST 2021 Conference Chair Message
publicationTitle: 2021 Third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies (TST)
abstract: On behalf of the TST 2021 organizing committee, I am honored to welcome you to the third International Conference on Transportation and Smart Technologies, Tangier, Morocco. I believe that no one can replace the face-to-face conference organization, but this edition was a successful conference, organized in virtual mode. The technical program was full, interesting and varied with four keynotes speakers, and around 18 technical full papers and 25 abstract papers programed on six parallel oral sessions during the conference days. In add, a very rich industrial round table was organized and focused on the digital services in the industry and the role of the AI in the transport and logistics.
